Diagnostic quicknotes (initial):
- Root candidate: KV cache evaporation after model variant:v2q introduced a slightly different tokenization leading to cache miss amplification for long-turn sessions. The eviction rate jumped ~3x at 08:58 (see attached sample: kv_cache_sample.log).
- Secondary: v2q quant path hits a slower matmul kernel variant on this GPU family at seq_len>256; that increases tail.
- Batching: Because of cache misses we observed smaller effective batch sizes, which compounds per-token latency.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
A) Rollback variant:v2q to v2 (fastest, conservative) — ~6m traffic shift + cache warmup 10–15m
B) Limit v2q to 10% and apply a routing policy to exclude BrightCart and other high-SLA tenants — buys time to patch heuristics
C) Increase burst node on shard 3 and apply targeted prefill of hot prefixes from last snapshot — costlier but preserves rollout

I recommend option A for safety. If Product insists on B, we can do B + targeted prefill (C). For either B/C we need a small runtime tweak: bump kv-cache-max-entries by 25% for shard 3 to reduce eviction pressure. That requires a rolling config change (no restart).

Attachments: kv_cache_sample.log (sample eviction trace), grafana_p99_surge.png

Diego Fernandez
SRE — Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Product/roadmap asks and operational constraints: 
- Short term (decide now): I support Diego's Option A (rollback). Product risk of rolling forward to v2q at this time is high given the tails and KV behavior. Rolling back reduces immediate customer risk.
- Mid term (roadmap 3–6w): Add a rollout heuristic to detect KV miss amplification and auto-throttle variant ramps based on per-tenant cache metrics. I'll file a ticket and assign to runtime team; want SRE/Eng input on thresholds.
- Exceptions: We need an exception panel to authorize routing policy overrides for top 20 customers (manual approval path). This is an ops+product policy item — Marissa, can you coordinate?

Customer comm guidance for BrightCart (Grace):
- Acknowledge detection and mitigation (we are reverting the recent rollout for their traffic)
- Explain expected customer impact: brief increase in request times while caches warm (~10–20m) and no functional change
- Offer to run a joint verification once we complete rollback and warmup

Related links: https://internal.incidents/redwood/INC-2028-0745

Subject: Brief update: gen-api p99 spike earlier today (what we changed, next steps)

Hi Jill —

Wanted to share a short update and the actions we took after our morning alert. We saw an elevated p99 on gen-api affecting a subset of traffic after a model variant rollout. Your traffic was routed to the variant for a brief period.

What we did:
- Rolled back the rollout for the variant causing the tail and pinned BrightCart traffic to the stable variant (v2) at 09:35 PDT.
- Applied cache warmup and increased capacity briefly to help tail recovery.

What to expect:
- You may have seen a small latency fluctuation this morning; performance should be back to baseline after a 10–20 minute warmup window.
- No data loss or request failures were introduced by our changes.

Next steps:
- We will run a short verification with your SRE team this afternoon to confirm steady-state. Diego has a diagnostic snapshot ready.
- Longer term we will add rollout heuristics to avoid this class of tail events and will share a timeline.

Apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience — we know time-to-recovery matters. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min sync at 16:30 PDT to walk through the snapshot.

Best,
Soojin Lee
